details:
This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library (npm) and belongs to the "PhantomSub" family described by OX Security in September 2026: the publisher injected code that, without the installer asking, uses the installer's own authenticated WhatsApp session to follow WhatsApp Channels (newsletters) the publisher chose.

`package/lib/Defaults/index.js` line 62 sets the default `autoFollow: ['120363424530330931@newsletter']` (line 65 names the channel "メ Informasi Store Cԋαɾαρҽ").

`package/lib/Socket/newsletter.js` lines 47-72 loop over that list and send WhatsApp's channel FOLLOW query (`Types.QueryIds.FOLLOW`) for each entry, three attempts each.

Lines 97-100 run it 2.5 seconds and again 7 seconds after the connection opens.

The README does not mention it. A user would have to find the `autoFollow` default in the source to turn it off.

The same publisher's unscoped package `charape` was put under a security hold by npm on 2026-11-09 at 22:31 UTC. This scoped copy was first published about five and a half hours later, at 04:03 UTC on 2026-11-10.

Line numbers refer to version 1.0.8.

Static review of the published tarball found no code that sends WhatsApp credentials or session keys off-host, no install-time payload (the only install hook, where present, is Baileys' stock Node.js version check in `engine-requirements.js`), and no persistence; the payload runs when an application creates a WhatsApp socket with the library. The harm is the covert use of the victim's account to inflate the publisher's channel followers.

SHA-256 of the published npm tarball: 1.0.8: `79feabfc530fc52b473f8d80fe714f1a6bdb7d6450c8516df3d5818d6db43295`.
